title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Lesergrenzen bewahren einen gemeinsamen Inhaltskern
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: ZL/IT/RF können dieselben lokalen Inhaltsbeziehungen mit unterschiedlicher Segmentierung oder Allographmarkierung bewahren; das ist eine Hypothese über Wortbildung und Leservarianten, keine Normalisierung der Fassungen.

design.scope_description: Only RF raw variants aligned to f77r.23, f80v.32/.36 and f85r1.4 plus the corresponding ZL3b/IT2a packet lines.
design.mechanism: Reader-specific spaces and marked characters alter surface segmentation while preserving a shared sequence of compositional kernels and local relation slots.
design.unit: Source-group aligned triples, retaining raw RF strings and separators rather than normalizing them.
design.contrast: Stable compositional spine under reader rendering versus independent lexical/segmentation alternatives.
design.prediction: The stable-spine account predicts invariant kernel order and relation-slot adjacency in f77r.23, f80v.32/.36 and f85r1.4 despite RF markings; the independent-reader account predicts materially different kernel or adjacency structures after alignment.
design.shared_mechanism: Surface allographs/spacing are a rendering layer over a shared content-building sequence; raw boundaries remain evidence, not errors.
concrete_observations: f77r.23 has ZL/IT olshedy qokeedy chedy qok[a:o]l/qokol but RF olshe@152;y qokeedy che@152;y qokal.
f80v.32 splits ZL arolkeedy while IT has arol keedy, and f85r1.4 changes ZL/IT olshedy qokeedy to RF olshe@152;y qokee@152;y.
linked_consequences: Aligned kernel order should survive the marked RF spellings without treating RF as a third independent paragraph.
A stable spine should predict the same local content relation in at least two loci, while preserving unresolved qok[a:o]l/qokol/qokal differences as an explicit terminal rival.
design.nearest_rival: Each transcription records an independent lexical segmentation, so apparent common forms are editorial convergence or coincidence.
design.distinguishing_observation: Publish a source-group alignment that lists raw strings, boundaries and invariant stems; a positive discriminator requires two loci with identical ordered kernel slots and one locus where the reader boundary differs, not a majority vote.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The apparent spine is inherited from transcriber conventions or broad high-frequency forms; f77r.23 has only one clear terminal variant and f85r1.4 RF leaves most content unresolved.
